title: Cohomology is computed after hypercover refinement
statement:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$, an abelian etale sheaf $F$,
and $q\geq0$, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \varinjlim_{U}H^q(C^\bullet(U,F))
 \xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(X_{\Et},F).
$$

The limit is over refinements, modulo simplicial homotopy, of the hypercovers
finite in each degree [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. The right side
is the derived cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. A
representative, and a relation between representatives, use only finitely
many degrees. The same assertion holds for sheaves of modules over a fixed
constant ring, with cohomology derived in that module category.

proof.text: The abelian and constant-ring module sheaf categories have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $F\hookrightarrow I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$. It is K-injective by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so $H^q(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet))$ is the group in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For a finite split hypercover $U$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover], put $D^{p,r}=I^r(U_p)$ and use the total differential $d(x)=\delta x+(-1)^p d_Ix$ on $D^{p,r}$. Each total degree has only finitely many bidegrees, so its totalization uses a finite direct sum.

source.place: Theorem 01H0 (theorem-cohomology-hypercoverings), comparison with injective sheaf cohomology; injective resolutions from Injectives, Theorem 01DU (theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives)

proof.text: For each injective $I^r$, [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-free-resolution] identifies the horizontal cohomology of $I^r(U_\bullet)$ with $I^r(X)$ in degree zero and zero in higher degrees. The horizontal-first spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] therefore has only its degree-zero column; its remaining differential is $d_I$ on $I^\bullet(X)$. Its finite filtration in each total degree shows that the augmentation $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}D$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The maps $F(U_p)\to I^0(U_p)$ define a cochain map $C^\bullet(U,F)\to\operatorname{Tot}D$: its vertical component vanishes because $F=\ker(I^0\to I^1)$. Thus we obtain a map $H^q(C^\bullet(U,F))\to H^q(X_{\Et},F)$, compatible with refinements and maps of sheaves.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: augmented injective double complex; compare Stacks 01H0 (theorem-cohomology-hypercoverings)

proof.text: For surjectivity, let $z=\sum_{p+r=q}z^{p,r}$ be a total cocycle. If $q>0$, its component $z^{0,q}$ is $d_I$-closed. Exactness of the sheaf resolution says that $I^{q-1}\to\ker(d_I:I^q\to I^{q+1})$ is an epimorphism; by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] its sections lift on an etale cover of each component of $U_0$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement] to make these finitely many local lifts into sections on a refinement and subtract the total boundary of a cochain in bidegree $(0,q-1)$, with the sign chosen to cancel $z^{0,q}$. Inductively, if components $(0,q),\ldots,(p-1,q-p+1)$ vanish, the bidegree $(p,q-p+1)$ cocycle equation makes $z^{p,q-p}$ vertically closed. When $q-p>0$, lift it locally through $I^{q-p-1}\to\ker d_I$, refine, and subtract the total boundary of a cochain in bidegree $(p,q-p-1)$; its horizontal term affects only bidegree $(p+1,q-p-1)$, so earlier zeros persist. After $p=q-1$, only $z^{q,0}$ remains. Its vertical differential is zero, so it is a section of $F(U_q)$, and its horizontal differential is zero, so it is a Cech cocycle. If $q=0$, the original total cocycle is already a section of $F(U_0)$ satisfying the Cech cocycle equation. This proves surjectivity after passage to refinements.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: successive removal of positive vertical degrees; compare Stacks 01H0 (theorem-cohomology-hypercoverings), first proof, successive killing of obstruction classes

proof.text: For injectivity in degree $q>0$, let $a\in F(U_q)$ be a Cech cocycle whose image in total cohomology vanishes. After a common refinement if needed, choose $b=\sum_{p+r=q-1}b^{p,r}$ with $db=a$. If $q>1$, $b^{0,q-1}$ is vertically closed because $db$ has no positive vertical component. Lift it locally from $I^{q-2}$, refine using [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement] and [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], and subtract a total boundary from $b$. Repeat with $(p,q-1-p)$ while its vertical degree is positive; the horizontal part of each correction affects only the next bidegree. At the end $b=b^{q-1,0}$, and the positive-vertical component of $db=a$ says $d_Ib=0$. Hence $b\in F(U_{q-1})$ and $a=\delta b$ after refinement. For $q=1$, this final argument applies directly to the sole component $b^{0,0}$. For $q=0$ there are no degree-minus-one boundaries, and $F(U_0)\hookrightarrow I^0(U_0)$ is injective. Thus a class mapping to zero vanishes in the colimit.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: injectivity by successive corrections of a total primitive; compare Stacks 01H0 (theorem-cohomology-hypercoverings), first proof, injectivity paragraph

proof.text: The homotopy category of finite split hypercovers is cofiltered by [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement]. Thus two representatives of the same derived class have a common refinement, where their difference maps to zero, and step 4 makes that difference a boundary after another refinement. The same node's prism identity makes homotopic refinement maps equal on cohomology, so the maps of step 2 define the displayed colimit map. The construction is natural in $F$: a map of sheaves extends to a map between injective resolutions up to chain homotopy [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and homotopic maps induce the same cohomology map. Each calculation involves only $U_0,\ldots,U_{q+1}$ (and a primitive through $q-1$), with finite choices at each refinement stage as in [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. For $R$-module sheaves, choose the resolution in that module category [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and use the free-module assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-free-resolution]. The module epimorphisms used for local lifts remain epimorphisms of underlying abelian sheaves because the forgetful functor is exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], then [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] supplies those lifts. The same finite corrections prove the module clause.
